title: Spectral Core-Tail Architecture for Locally Certified Gibbs-State Preparation
abstract: Preparing a quantum Gibbs state requires reproducing both its thermal distribution and the associated many-body eigenspaces. In this work, we formalize the spectral core-tail architecture (SCTA) as a framework comprising a structured thermal core, a geometrically characterized unitary tail, and an exact residual measuring the remaining core-frame Hamiltonian mismatch. We derive a local Gibbs-state error bound separating core-preparation, tail-implementation, and modeling errors. The modeling contribution is volume uniform when its Kubo-Mori response meets the shell summability condition and the relevant local data remain uniform. We then highlight three anchor Hamiltonian classes which admit exact core-tail constructions with zero residuals. For small deformations of an exact anchor, we employ a Schrieffer-Wolff reduction procedure to construct a corrected core-tail pair that formally removes the deformation order by order. Under uniform locality and solvability assumptions, we show that the first-order reduction yields a residual that remains bounded and is quadratic in the deformation strength. Furthermore, we numerically test the first-order reduction on deformed graph-stabilizer Hamiltonians. The numerical results show approximately quadratic suppression of both the Hamiltonian-level mismatch and the local Gibbs-state error in the perturbative regime. We also find that the constructed correction circuit structure remains useful as a variational ansatz beyond perturbative control, often improving on both the bare and prescribed first-order states.
summary: This paper introduces the Spectral Core-Tail Architecture (SCTA) as a systematic framework for preparing quantum Gibbs states. It rigorously analyzes the error sources by decomposing the problem into a core, a tail, and a residual. The key achievement is demonstrating that controlled, perturbative corrections can suppress preparation errors quadratically, offering a powerful tool for simulating thermal states in complex quantum systems.
main_problem: The central problem is developing a framework to prepare a quantum Gibbs state, $ho_ eta(H)$, which requires accurately reproducing both the thermal distribution and the underlying many-body eigenspaces.
main_result: The authors introduce the Spectral Core-Tail Architecture (SCTA) and show that for small deformations of exact anchor Hamiltonians, the resulting Hamiltonian mismatch and local Gibbs-state error suppress quadratically in the perturbative regime.
method: The methodology involves decomposing the state preparation into a structured thermal core, a unitary tail, and an error residual, followed by applying a Schrieffer-Wolff-type local reduction procedure for perturbative corrections.
model_or_system: The work is general for quantum many-body systems described by a Hamiltonian $H$, but specific tests involve inhomogeneous transverse-field Ising chains (free-fermionic) and graph-stabilizer Hamiltonians.

main_assumptions: Assumptions include uniform locality, solvability, and the ability to control the response envelope via shell summability for error bounding.

paper_structure: The paper is structured around developing the operational framework (SCTA), identifying exact anchor Hamiltonians, applying perturbative deformations via local reduction, and concluding with numerical and variational tests.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, structured approach to state preparation for thermal equilibrium states, which is fundamental to understanding quantum dynamics and thermalization in many-body systems.
